- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often overshoots early in forecast horizon; cap peak forecasts at 2–3% below recent high.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overcorrects downward; apply a 1–2% upward bias to offset mean reversion.  
- When sentiment swings from positive to negative, model often fails to adjust quickly; delay downward correction by 1–2 periods.  
- If forecast mean is >85 and true outcome is <80, model exhibits horizon bias; reduce forecast by 5–10% for 3–5 period ahead.  
- Sentiment volatility >0.33 in 3 consecutive days → model overfits noise; apply smoothing filter to reduce forecast variance.
